title: Feit–Thompson Odd Order Theorem Formally Verified End-to-End in Coq (170,000 Lines)
whyItMatters: First complete machine-checked formalization of a monumental modern pure-mathematics proof—170,000 lines of Coq verifying the 255-page 1963 Odd Order Theorem, foundational pillar of finite simple group classification.
summary: Completed on September 20, 2012 by Georges Gonthier and a 15-researcher Microsoft Research–INRIA team (published at ITP 2013), this six-year effort produced a complete, kernel-checked Coq formalization of the Feit–Thompson Odd Order Theorem—that every finite group of odd order is solvable. Unlike the Four Color Theorem, Feit–Thompson’s 255-page 1963 proof was pure abstract algebra spanning finite group theory, character theory, and Galois theory. The formalization required ~170,000 lines of Coq, ~4,200 definitions, and ~15,000 lemmas, creating the Mathematical Components (MathComp) library and proving deep modern algebra could be formally machine-verified.
technicalHighlights: Verified the entire 255-page 1963 Odd Order Theorem from foundational axioms using ~170,000 lines of Coq/SSReflect code.
Built the reusable Mathematical Components (MathComp) algebraic hierarchy library covering group theory, linear algebra, and character theory.
Provided the historical benchmark for formalizing deep finite-group theory, directly preceding 2026 autonomous Lean CFSG formalizations.
caveats: Required six years of manual interactive formalization by a large team using Coq’s symbolic tactics rather than autonomous AI proof synthesis.

scoreRationale.foundational: Proved that deep, book-length modern pure mathematics—not just combinatorial case splits—could be completely machine-verified.
scoreRationale.ripple: Directly inspired mathlib in Lean and set the blueprint for large-scale formalized algebra.
scoreRationale.verification: 100% machine-checked inside Coq’s trusted symbolic kernel.
scoreRationale.velocity: Took 6 years of expert effort, establishing the human-era pace baseline before LLM+Lean autoformalization.
